newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spot Prods - Gulf, Midco gasolines strengthen.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spot Prods - Gulf, Midco gasolines strengthen.

text.p: U.S. Gulf (USG) and midcontinent gasoline differentials firmed by late Wednesday, helped by the constructive inventory data and rumors of refinery problems.

On the NYMEX, June gasoline futures gained 0.61 cent by the close, boosted by the 3.6 million barrel draw in gasoline stocks shown in the weekly American Petroleum Institute (API) data. June heating oil futures ended down 0.45 cent.
Concerns about possible output problems at one of Amoco's Gulf facilities may have lent a bullish tone to the market, though market players noticed no unusual buying activity in the spot markets.
++ Gasoline. Regular unleaded "M1" gasoline began firming early in the day, confirmed deals seen as strong as 3.40 cents under the June futures, up almost 0.50 cent on the day.
Prompt reformulated A1 gasoline was also talked at higher levels, traders said, with barrels seen between 2.15 and 2.40 cents under the June futures.

++ Gasoline. Regular reformulated A1 gasoline values popped up a touch, with offers heard 0.10 cent higher at a cent over June futures, helped by the 2.0 million barrel drop in RFG stocks shown in the API data.
++ Group Three prompt unleaded gasoline differentials rose by a cent to 2.75 to 3.00 cent over the June NYMEX futures, also helped by talk of potential output problems at Amoco.
Prompt Chicago differentials for gasoline gained 0.25 cent to sit 0.75 to 1.00 cent over the June NYMEX.
